turnaround_reason: Charter cratered (~48% off highs, 'worst day ever' in 2026) as broadband subscriber losses accelerated under fixed-wireless and fiber competition. The bull case rests on the just-closed $34.5B Cox merger, huge FCF, and a rock-bottom multiple; the bear case is a secular broadband melt on a mountain of debt.
bullish_points: Cox merger closed ($34.5B) — creates the largest US broadband/video provider, ~37M customers across 45 states, with synergy and scale upside
Deep value on cash earnings: trailing P/E 3.8, forward 3.3; EV/EBITDA 5.5; FCF $2.2B and operating cash flow $16.5B
Mobile is a genuine growth vector (12M+ lines and climbing), partially offsetting broadband erosion
Street mean target (~$184) sits well above spot ($147), implying material upside if losses stabilize
bearish_points: Broadband bleeding: -172k subs in Q2 2026 (worse than -120k in Q1) — the trend is deteriorating, not stabilizing
Crushing leverage: total debt $96.7B, debt/equity 441%, current ratio 0.36 — equity is a thin sliver on a huge capital structure
Cox integration risk layered on top of an already-pressured core; merger timing/synergy realization uncertain
Analyst split skews cautious (more Holds/Sells than Buys); FCF inflection could slip if ARPU compresses
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings (Oct 30) — first look at broadband-sub trajectory and early Cox integration; any sign losses are stabilizing would re-rate the equity given the low multiple
suggested_trade: Watchlist / very small starter only. Wait for evidence broadband losses are stabilizing (a single quarter of moderation) before committing real size; the leverage makes this a knife until the trend turns.
key_risk: Broadband subscriber losses keep accelerating, so ARPU compression delays the FCF inflection and the 441% debt load re-rates the thin equity sharply lower.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows broadband losses widening again or Cox integration stumbles; only turns actionable once sub losses visibly moderate.
